_comment: Alert definitions to create in OpenObserve (Alerts -> Add alert). Stream: network_syslog (the only stream; ~1.6B events). Fields seen on EfficientIP rows: host, hostname, device, appname (dhcpd, named, ipmserver, ...), facility, collector, message. DHCP and DNS run on hera.middlebury.edu and lion.middlebury.edu (lion is believed to be zeus; juno and jupiter are the management appliances). Each alert is created twice: a firing alert (this query, shared template 'keep-efficientip-firing') and a cleared alert named '<alert_name> (cleared)' (same query, threshold 'less than 1', using its own cleared template whose fingerprint hard-codes '<alert_name>'). See docs/efficientip-openobserve.md. Query results below were measured against real data on 2026-10-07.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'dhcpd' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND match_all('no free leases') AND message NOT LIKE '%default-netv4%' AND message NOT LIKE '%efault-netv4%' ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: WITHOUT the default-netv4 exclusion this matches ~27,000 lines/day (hera and lion answering DHCPDISCOVER on their own interface for the built-in default-netv4 network): never alert on the raw pattern. WITH the exclusions: 6 events in 30 days, 5 of them a real burst on 2026-09-28 10:07 on hera (relay 140.233.107.1, 'cancel load balance to peer failover-dhcp1-smart.middlebury.edu - no free leases').
alerts.note: dhcpd logs the network name, so this is already per shared network. The card shows the most recent matching line.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'dhcpd' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND (match_all('exiting') OR match_all('failed') OR match_all('not running')) ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: 1 match in 30 days. Quiet enough, but read that one line first to confirm it is a real fault pattern before enabling.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'named' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND match_all('failed') AND match_all('exiting') ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: 0 matches in 30 days. named does log from both hosts (about 2.4M and 1.3M lines/day), so silence may just mean nothing broke, but the wording is unverified. Find a real named failure line before relying on this.

alerts.sql: SELECT host, message FROM "network_syslog" WHERE appname = 'named' AND host IN ('hera.middlebury.edu','lion.middlebury.edu') AND match_all('zone') AND (match_all('not loaded') OR match_all('has errors') OR match_all('loading failed')) ORDER BY _timestamp DESC LIMIT 1
alerts.measured: 0 matches in 30 days. Same caveat as DNS Service Failed: wording unverified.
